acceptance_criteria: AC-1 Every numbered clause of the four documents that concerns backup appears in the audit with exactly one of the four verdicts.
AC-2 An IMPLEMENTED verdict names the file and, where it exists, the test; a NOT_IMPLEMENTED verdict names what is absent rather than merely asserting absence.
AC-3 Every clause is checked for the join, not only for the presence of one half.
AC-4 Findings are ordered by consequence, with the ordering justified.
AC-5 The document's status line reads DRAFT -- AUDIT, NOT AUTHORITY, and it changes no other file.
AC-6 No configuration value, address, hostname, serial, credential or artefact content appears in the document; the repository privacy gate passes.

baseline.authority: The four documents in refs, all FROZEN: 14H (the backup step, the pilot allowlist, the asynchronous submit-then-poll truth), 14I (where artefacts live, how an operator reads one, deviation, management servers), 14K (a backup creation is not a recovery write and is console-submittable), and C7 (the artefact and restore engine contract, with restore disabled). AGENTS.md's authority hierarchy makes a FROZEN document implementation law; this audit measures how far the implementation actually goes.
baseline.engineering_baseline: The Java product lives under ui2/: service, worker, persistence and frontend modules, with migrations under ui2/service/src/main/resources/db/migration. The Python tree at the repository root is the earlier line and is not the audit's subject.
baseline.product_baseline: Check Point gateway backup is implemented end to end and gated to a pilot allowlist that is currently empty. The device workspace lists retained artefacts with their deviation state, an operator can request a backup with a reason, collection is refused against a management server, and a configuration run carries a structural deviation summary. Every live outcome is UNVERIFIED: no feature in this product has yet reached a real device.
baseline.test_baseline: The ui2 suites and the repository privacy gate pass on origin/main today.
baseline.what_exists:
The gap that motivated this audit, as an example of the shape being hunted: UI2_0_C3's gate table required a CSRF token on every state-changing method and the sessions schema declared `csrf_secret TEXT NOT NULL`. The token was minted, stored and required -- and never returned to the client in any response or cookie, so every write was refused with 401 SESSION_INVALID. The frontend's own file header described the gap as `a disclosed, temporary limitation` and named a movement that never closed it. No test failed, because no test asserted that a browser could obtain a token it was obliged to send.

That is the pattern: a clause whose two halves were each implemented by a different movement, with nothing testing the join.

invariants: Read only. One new file, nothing else touched.
Evidence over assertion: a verdict names where it looked.
Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence -- NOT_EVALUABLE exists so a clause that cannot be checked from the repository is not silently called implemented.
No secret, identity or device value enters the document.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker opens the pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Find the clauses the backup line claims and does not have. On 2026-09-15 it emerged that every write in the product was being refused, because the CSRF token the gate required was never returned to the client -- a gap that had been written down in a source comment and never closed, while every test stayed green and the product looked healthy. This audit looks for the same shape of gap across the frozen backup contracts: a clause that is frozen, believed implemented, and is not actually wired, or is wired with nothing testing it. Read only. Change nothing.
output_contract: A list of what the backup line promises and does not yet do, ordered by what it would cost to be wrong.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A cross-module reading task whose value is in following each clause to its join, which is where the last failure of this shape hid.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Both commands run from the repository root.
Run only the commands named above. Do not build, do not run the Java or frontend suites; this is a reading task.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before committing and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
A mechanical mismatch between this packet and the code is settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE gives the verdict counts, names the three findings you consider most consequential, and says which clauses you could not evaluate and why.
risks: Calling a clause implemented because a symbol with the right name exists, without following it to a caller -- the exact failure that let the write path stay broken.
Grepping for a keyword and concluding absence when the implementation uses different words; look for the behaviour, not the phrase.
Drifting into fixing what is found, which turns a read-only audit into an unreviewed change.
Padding the document with restated contract text instead of findings.

in: Read the four contracts and enumerate their numbered clauses -- 14H BK-n, 14I AL-n/DV-n/OR-n/RC-n/MS-n, 14K BW-n, and C7's own numbered obligations for backup (not restore, which is disabled).

For each clause, find the code that implements it and the test that holds it. Report one of four verdicts per clause: IMPLEMENTED_AND_TESTED with the file and test named; IMPLEMENTED_UNTESTED with the file named and the missing assertion described; NOT_IMPLEMENTED with what is absent; or NOT_EVALUABLE with the reason the clause cannot be checked from the repository alone.

Say explicitly, for every clause, whether both halves of it are joined -- a producer with no consumer, a field written and never read, a guard required and never satisfiable, are the failures this audit exists to catch.
Write the findings to docs/design/BACKUP_LINE_IMPLEMENTATION_AUDIT_2026_09_15.md with a status line of DRAFT -- AUDIT. NOT AUTHORITY. It records findings; it decides nothing and freezes nothing.
Order the findings by consequence: a clause whose absence would let something unsafe happen first, a clause whose absence merely leaves a feature incomplete last. Say which is which and why.
out: Changing any code, any test, any contract or any project data. This movement writes exactly one new file and nothing else.
Restore. C7 keeps it disabled and this audit does not examine, propose or prepare it.
Contacting a device, running the product, or reading any credential, artefact or database content.

Judging whether a frozen clause is a good decision. The audit measures implementation against the clause as written; disagreeing with a clause is a Product Owner matter and belongs in the SESSION_CLOSE, not in a verdict.
Opening backlog items or editing project/*.json. Findings go in the document; the Product Owner decides what becomes work.
